critical_steps: The underlying identity analysis family is Parseval.
P has eigenvalues 2 and 1; Q has eigenvalues 39/20 and 1/20, so both controls are positive invertible.
The controlled quadratic form equals 2 x^2 + (57/20) x y + y^2 and takes the exact value -1/40 at (1,-3/2).
For a general ordinary continuous g-frame, the controlled quadratic form is represented by Q S_Lambda P.
The two-sided controlled inequality is equivalent to Q S_Lambda P being positive invertible.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact one-point continuous g-frame on real two-dimensional Hilbert space with two explicit positive noncommuting controls.
integrity.unproved_limits: No weakest algebraic condition on P and Q alone, uniformly over every possible frame operator, is classified beyond the stated exact per-frame operator criterion.

limitations: The result refutes the unrestricted converse in Theorem 2.1 and the universal-control assertion in Corollary 2.2.
Pairwise commutation of the controls and frame operator is sufficient but not claimed necessary.
No classification of unrelated dual-frame statements in the source is asserted.

title: Noncommuting positive controls can destroy a continuous \(g\)-frame
